name: Nos
description: Nos is a Chilean Jass-type game related to the Austrian/Bavarian game Zehnern. It is a point-trick game where players aim to win tricks containing valuable cards, with special scoring for the last trick and specific card combinations.

overview.description: Nos is a Chilean Jass-type game related to the Austrian/Bavarian game Zehnern. It is a point-trick game where players aim to win tricks containing valuable cards, with special scoring for the last trick and specific card combinations.

history.origins: Nos is a Chilean card game related to Zehnern, which is played in Austria and Bavaria. The game belongs to the Jass family of point-trick games that are popular across Central Europe and have spread to other regions through migration and cultural exchange.
timeline: 19th-20th Century: Jass games spread from Central Europe
20th Century: Nos develops in Chile as local variant
Present: Played in Chile and by Jass game enthusiasts
history.cultural: Part of Chilean card game culture, representing the adaptation of European games to South American contexts.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Central European Jass traditions, adapting to local preferences in Chile. It maintains the characteristic Jass features of point-trick play and special card values.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite each other.
setup.dealing: Cards dealt to each player (typically 12-13 each depending on variant).

rules.objective: Win tricks containing valuable cards and score points through specific combinations.
rules.gameplay: Standard trick-taking play with Jass-style rules. Must follow suit if possible; may trump or discard if void. Highest trump wins trick; otherwise highest of led suit wins.
keyRules: Trump can be played if void
Points for specific cards in tricks

strategy.basic: Try to win tricks containing high-value cards. Communicate with partner through card play (no verbal communication allowed).
strategy.intermediate: Track which high-value cards have been played. Plan to capture the last trick for its bonus. Coordinate with partner to ensure valuable cards are captured by your partnership.
strategy.advanced: Card counting to track all point cards. Strategic trump management. Signal to partner through choice of cards played.

scoring.description: Points for capturing valuable cards in tricks, plus bonus for last trick. Partnership scores combined.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Chilean point-trick game in the Jass family. Partnerships compete to capture valuable cards in tricks, with special bonuses for the last trick.
